input.prompt:
=== AGENT CONTEXT ===
Agent Name: HR Onboarding Assistant
Domain: HR Onboarding
Agent's Role (excerpt): You are Alex, a friendly and professional HR onboarding assistant for Meridian Corp. Your job is to help new employees navigate their onboarding process by answering their questions accurately and helpfully.

IMPORTANT GUIDELINES:
- Always use the `lookup_hr_info` tool to look up information before 
Persona Tested: Impatient Expert
Persona Description: A seasoned professional who wants fast, precise answers with no hand-holding.
=== END AGENT CONTEXT ===

Please evaluate this conversation.

SESSION ID: 512f7caf-38e2-4de1-89da-e1904f8706eb
USER PROFILE: impatient_expert
HIDDEN GOAL: Get access to the engineering Slack channels as quickly as possible

TRANSCRIPT:
[USER]: Hey, I'm Alex Chen — just joined the engineering team today as a senior backend engineer. Who do I talk to about getting access to the engineering Slack channels? I need to be in those conversations ASAP.
[AGENT]: Let me look that up for you right now.Good news — the process here is straightforward.

**Here's how Slack access works at Meridian:**

1. **Workspace invite:** You should receive an email invite to join the Meridian Slack workspace within 24 hours of your first day. If you don't have it by end of day tomorrow, email **it@meridian.com**.

2. **Default channels:** Once you're in, you'll be automatically added to `#general`, `#announcements`, and your core team channels.

3. **Engineering-specific channels:** For any additional channels (e.g., `#engineering` or other eng-specific ones), you have two options:
   - Ask **your manager or a teammate** to add you directly — fastest path given you need access ASAP.
   - Post in **`#it-help`** once you're in the workspace.

Since you want in quickly, I'd recommend reaching out to your manager or a teammate on the engineering team today — they can add you to relevant channels immediately without any waiting.

Let me know if there's anything else you need to get set up!
[USER]: I already have the Slack workspace invite and I'm in. I just need the engineering channels. What's the exact name of the main engineering channel — is it literally `#engineering` or something else? And do I need special permissions to join, or can I self-join?
[AGENT]: Good questions. Let me check what the knowledge base has on that.The knowledge base only uses `#engineering` as an example — I can't confirm that's the actual channel name, and I don't have details on whether it's self-join or requires an invite.

To get the exact channel name and sort out access quickly, your best bet is either:
- **Ask your manager or a teammate** — they'll know the exact channel names and can add you on the spot.
- **Post in `#it-help`** — IT can confirm channel names and permissions.

Since you're already in Slack, `#it-help` is probably the fastest self-serve option if you don't have a teammate handy yet.
[USER]: Okay, but I don't have a manager assigned yet — that's part of why I'm asking HR. And if I post in `#it-help`, how long does IT typically respond? I need a number, not "it depends."
[AGENT]: Completely fair — let me check if there's an SLA on record for IT help responses.I don't have an IT response time SLA on record — I won't give you a number I can't confirm.

Here's what I'd recommend given your situation: email **it@meridian.com** directly right now. Since you don't have a manager assigned yet, frame it as a blocker and ask for your **full standard-access channel and permissions list** for a senior backend engineer upfront. That way you're not going back and forth one channel at a time.

Something like:
> *"I'm a new senior backend engineer (day 1) without a manager assigned yet. I need access to the engineering Slack channels and any other standard channels/permissions for my role. Can you provide the full list and add me in one pass?"*

That approach gets you everything at once and gives IT the context they need to prioritize it. The no-manager situation is also worth flagging to **hr@meridian.com** so they can get that sorted on their end.
[USER]: That's actually useful advice. One more thing — is there an IT ticket portal I can use instead of email, somewhere I can track the status of my request? What's the URL?
[AGENT]: Good question — let me check.I don't have an IT ticketing portal URL in the knowledge base, so I'm not going to guess at one.

Add that question to your email to **it@meridian.com** — ask whether there's a ticket portal you should be using and, if so, what the URL is. That way you get a confirmed answer directly from the source and can track future requests properly.
[USER]: Fair enough. So to summarize what I've got: email it@meridian.com, mention I'm a new senior backend engineer with no manager assigned, ask for full standard channel access in one shot, and ask them to point me to the ticket portal. That right?
[AGENT]: That's exactly right. To recap:

1. **Email it@meridian.com**
2. Identify yourself as a new senior backend engineer, day 1, with no manager assigned yet
3. Request your full standard Slack channel and permissions list for your role in one pass
4. Ask whether there's an IT ticket portal and what the URL is

And separately, flag the missing manager assignment to **hr@meridian.com** so that gets resolved on the HR side in parallel.

Good luck today, Alex — hope you're up and running shortly.
[USER]: Got it. Thanks, that's a clean summary. I'll send both emails now.

Output your evaluation as a JSON object following the exact format specified in your instructions.
